resolves: WIRE_REFERENCE.md UNVERIFIED item 4 — the PKI/DM scheme
method: We published an X25519 public key for a synthetic node via NodeInfo, then drove the stock node's own API to send that node a text. The resulting frame was captured off the air by our receiver and decrypted with the matching private key.

scheme.kdf: SHA-256 over the raw X25519 shared secret
scheme.key_size: 32 bytes — the full SHA-256 output, NOT truncated to 128 bits
scheme.nonce: 13 bytes: packet_id (u32 LE) || extra_nonce (4 bytes) || from (u32 LE) || 0x00
scheme.channel_hash: 0x00 — this is how a PKI packet is distinguished on the wire

behaviour_notes: A stock node uses PKI for direct messages by default and REFUSES to fall back to channel encryption when the destination's public key is unknown: 'Unknown public key for destination node ..., refusing to send legacy DM'. A node that has not published a key cannot be sent a DM at all.
The node must have learned the key in the CURRENT boot; a freshly learned node lost across a reset takes the key with it.
